The version a row's last execution carried out, rebuilt from the log

log_executed_row.Rd

Every intent field as the round read it when it last carried the row out, accepted only when its seal, request_seal(), is the one the channel wrote at that execution, log_executions(). The seal proves the reading: a version rebuilt wrong does not give the channel's seal, and the answer is then NULL, never a value that may be wrong.

Usage

log_executed_row(events, record, channel_account = NULL)

Arguments

events

The event log, as register_log() returns it.

record

The record id to look at.

channel_account

The REDCap usernames that hold the round's token, one or more, or NULL when they are not configured: then every write of the seal counts as an execution, as for log_executions().

Value

NULL when the row was never carried out in its current life, the channel is not known, log_channel_unknown(), or no cut gives the channel's seal. Otherwise a list: row, a data frame of one row holding record_id and every intent field as carried out; seal, the seal it gives; at, the position of the execution in log_of_record(); cut, the position of the cut, the newest event the version holds.

Details

How it is rebuilt, decided on 2026-11-12. The round reads the register, then the identity door writes the username it resolved, then the round carries the row out and writes the seal, which covers the row as read with the resolved name in place of the one read. In the log, between the execution before (or the creation) and the newest one, stand the writes the round read and, above them, those made while it ran, by anybody. So the version carried out is the state of the log at a cut below the seal:

  • each intent field holds the newest write at the cut or below it, in the row's current life, log_of_record(), by anybody, the channel included; a field never written is ""; record_id is the record;

  • username holds instead the channel's write between the cut and the seal, when there is one: the identity door of the round that carried the row out, written after the reading;

  • the cuts are tried from the highest (right below the seal, no write left out) to the lowest (right above the execution before), and the first whose seal is the channel's is the answer. Two cuts that both give the channel's seal give the same values, so which one is taken does not matter.

A write made before the reading is carried out whoever made it, with or without an approval; one made after it is not, whoever made it: the owner's own write while the round ran, the person written while it ran, a revocation written while it ran. Who approved what is not needed.

The values are read with log_written_value(), whole up to the apostrophe that closes them, and brought to the form of the register by log_value_as_register(). A value the log holds in another form makes no cut give the seal, and the answer is NULL: the row is not verified, and no value is guessed. Measured on 2026-11-12 on the live register (M1 and M1b): the reconstruction gives the channel's seal on every row whose seal did not move, once the field names inside Read back as are no longer read as writes (log_field_at()); non-ASCII letters, capitals in an address, spaces at the edges of the register's values and fields never written among them. Not measured yet: apostrophes, & < > and quotes, dates written by the form, a project_id with a leading zero, values longer than 100 characters, emptied fields.

No intent field is a checkbox. One that were would be logged as field(code) = checked, and this function would have to learn it first.
